candidates.source_title: Rochdale 1-0 Swindon - Sky Sports
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Cian Hayes headed a late winner as Rochdale capitalised on Swindon having a man sent off to secure a 1-0 victory and increase the pressure on Ian Holloway.

Under-fire Robins' boss Holloway branded himself a "dead man walking" in a viral pre-match interview but his side looked to have done enough to secure a welcome point at the Crown Oil Arena.

But Kaelan Majekodunmi was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 85th minute and Rochdale struck three minutes later to snatch the points as Hayes glanced home Aden Flint's knock-on.

Neither goalkeeper had been seriously tested in the opening half, though it took Flint's timely intervention to prevent Anthony Munda's low drive from troubling Nils Ramming in the Rochdale goal.

After the interval, Antwoine Hackford was denied by Ramming while Rochdale frontman Dajaune Brown missed a golden opportunity in the 66th minute when he got his feet in a tangle and failed to convert Glenn Middleton's inviting delivery.

Brown saw a volleyed effort pushed over the bar by Connor Ripley, who later saved brilliantly from Charlie Tasker before Hayes delivered the decisive blow.

candidates.source_title: Ian Holloway praises injury-hit Swindon’s effort after late loss at Rochdale - The Herald
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Swindon boss Ian Holloway praised his injury-hit squad’s performance despite a 1-0 defeat at Rochdale. The under-fire Robins boss, who described himself as a “dead man walking” during a viral interview in the build-up to the game, felt his patched-up side deserved a share of the spoils. But Cian Hayes headed the winning goal in the 88th minute for Rochdale, three minutes after the dismissal of Kaelan Majekodunmi for a second bookable offence. “I thought it was a fantastic performance from the lads and the game turned on a couple of moments,” said Holloway. “Were the bookings really bookings? And then the ball has hit someone in the face and they score. It’s just the way it’s gone for us. “We had two good chances in the second half and we had to take one of them. Had we done that, it’s a different game. “The lads worked their socks off and it’s fine margins. One of our lads gets smashed in the head. He’s having treatment and they go and score! “It’s an absolutely rubbish rule, not everybody is cheating and lying down waiting for treatment. Why don’t they use their common sense and change the rules? My centre half is off the field receiving treatment and it should be their bloke, the one who clobbered him, who should be off the field.

candidates.source_title: Blooming marvellous primary school celebrates second eco award! - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Heybrook Primary and Nursery School has been sowing the seeds of success after achieving its second Eco-Schools Award for its commitment to environmental education and sustainability. To mark this significant achievement and demonstrate its continued dedication to caring for the environment, pupils, staff and families came together to plant 1,000 spring bulbs across the school grounds. The community planting event welcomed parents, grandparents and other family members into school to work alongside children, helping to create vibrant displays that will bring colour and interest to the grounds in the months ahead while also supporting local biodiversity. The Eco-Schools Award recognises schools that empower young people to make a positive impact on the environment through sustainable education and action. candidates.source_title: 'Sickening' - Holloway frustrated as Swindon get no luck in defeat at Rochdale - Swindon Advertiser
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ian Holloway said that it was "sickening" for Swindon Town to lose 1-0 at Rochdale after what he felt was their best away performance. Swindon were without half of their squad at Rochdale, but turned in a strong display, and would have been disappointed not to be ahead after 70 minutes as they failed to make a few big chances count. But without reinforcements on the bench, the hosts came on strong, and two yellow cards for Kaelan Majekodunmi proved too much to contend with, and Cian Hayes headed in the winner with two minutes to play. Swindon had just 15 players to pick from for the game, and it could have been less than that after Joseph Hungbo had a niggle in his knee in training before travelling. That meant that even the substitutes were not fully fit, making it an even tougher task for Swindon to end their tough run away from home, where they are still yet to win or score. Holloway said that there was so much to like about what Swindon did, but they just let themselves down at the end. He said: "That is sickening for everybody. "When you put your lives on the line like that lads did today, and there were some fantastic performances, it is tough to take.

candidates.source_title: Warsaw Uprising exhibition launched at Bury’s Fusilier Museum
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An exhibition about the Warsaw Uprising of 1944 was launched at the Fusilier Museum in Bury on Thursday evening, October 1. Warsaw Calling: Uprising 1944 explores the Polish underground resistance’s uprising against Nazi occupation, which began on August 1, 1944. Resistance fighters and civilians fought for the liberation of Warsaw for 63 days. The exhibition uses personal stories, archival material and images to tell the stories of those who lived through the uprising. It was curated by the Polish Underground Movement Study Trust in partnership with Polonia Northern England. A complementary display, Northern Heroines, tells the stories of three women connected to the Polish community in the North of England. It was produced by Polonia Northern England. Warsaw Calling: Uprising 1944 runs until February 27, 2027. Entry is included in museum admission. The museum is on Moss Street, Bury, BL9 0DF. Admission costs £4.95 for adults, £3.95 for concessions, £2.95 for children and £9.95 for families. Tickets include an annual pass allowing repeat visits for 12 months.

candidates.source_title: Details of new Scout Moor wind farm revealed
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A new wind farm planned for moorland between Rochdale and Bury has reduced in size, but it’s still not good enough for opposing campaigners. The Say NO to Scout Moor 2 group has objected to Cubico Sustainable Investments plan for ‘Scout Moor 2’ ever since they were first mooted back in 2024. Campaigners fear the turbines – up to 180m including blade tip height – would be larger than Blackpool Tower and dominate the skyline. The latest changes from Cubico have seen the scheme dropped from 17 wind turbines to 12. This reduction means that the proposed windfarm would only have the potential to power 84,552 homes annually, rather than 100,000 previously touted. There is already a wind farm in operation on Scout Moor. But according to planning documents, the farm would be run separately and have a life span of around 40 years. Planning papers also highlight the need for underground cables connected to an on-site substation, which will later be hooked up to a supply point in Rossendale to deliver electricity to the National Grid. The clean energy generation from the turbines is said to recover the fossil fuel costs to build the new wind farm in 18 months. They’ve also said the excavation of peat, a pivotal carbon dioxide capture source, will be reduced by 28 per cent. Cubico has promised a peat restoration project so the extracted peat will not be lost entirely. This is something objectors don’t believe is realistic. Cubico also said they are avoiding placing turbines that dominate local viewpoints. But these statements have also been challenged by local campaigners.

candidates.source_title: Could the Turner Brothers factory finally be getting cleared up
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale. It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to keep six offices at a commercial unit have been refused because planners found “no evidence that the building had been used as offices”. Shahida Farooq applied to Rochdale Council for a certificate of lawfulness for six existing offices at Bridge House, Mellor Street, Rochdale. The property sits between Mellor Street and Spotland Road and was built over the River Spodden. It had previously been home to a private-hire booking office and light industrial use, both of which had planning permission. Mrs Farooq’s application says Bridge House has been occupied and operated as commercial offices for approximately 10 years or more, which would allow for a certificate of lawfulness to be issued. The application added: “Internal refurbishment work has commenced to subdivide the building into six individual commercial units. No material change of use has taken place as all units remain within Use Class E (offices).” A planning officer’s report stated: “There have been three planning applications associated with the site. Application 94/D30996 was for a change of use from Use Class B1 (Business Use) to Use Class B2 (General Industrial Use). Planning permission was granted subject to conditions. “Following this, there were two applications in 1999 for the use of the basement as a private-hire booking office and a retrospective application to site a portacabin for use as a private-hire booking office with associated parking and external water closet. “Google Streetview images from August, 2016, of the front elevation facing Mellor Street show that there were two units. The fascia signs read Langstreth & Hunter Accountancy Service and Conservatory & Garden Furniture.

candidates.source_title: Supermarkets criticised after trolleys end up in canal
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Aldi, Morrisons, and Tesco have been told to ‘get their act together’ by a litter picking group who keep having to haul supermarket trolleys out of a canal. Along a stretch of the Rochdale canal in Failsworth, litter picking group Clean Up Failsworth Canal said they regularly have to drag trolleys out of the water as part of their impressive efforts to clean up the area. The group, which has been running for over 13 years, goes out once a month. Armed with litter pickers and dozens of bags, the team regularly find flytipped rubbish, drinks cans, and nitrous oxide or ‘laughing gas’ cannisters. On September 20, around 22 bags of rubbish had been filled and 26 cannisters were collected while 17 trolleys were fished out of the canal. The trolleys, according to the group, are increasingly becoming a problem. In some areas such as under the bridge to the town’s Tesco car park, the dumped trolleys could even mean boats struggle to get through. Sandra Ball, who represents Failsworth West for Reform UK, said: “Tesco, Aldi, and Morrisons the other end need to get their act together and get it sorted. The trolleys have always been a problem. We have taken 20 out in one session.” She added: “At the end of the day, that cost comes back to us. They have got to pay for [new] trolleys.” Coun Ball has been involved with the group for years. Supported by Oldham council and the Canal and River Trust, she said around 90 people involved in her Failsworth litter busting team. Despite the efforts, she and others feel like it’s a ‘disheartening’ uphill battle, adding: “Within 10 minutes, someone else will have dropped something but if you do not keep on top of it, what would it look like?”

candidates.source_title: Homes powered by Baked Beans could be part of Greater Manchester’s future
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major plan is being developed that could power thousands of homes with the heat from baked beans, sewage, and data centres. EnergiRaven, a UK-based green energy transition consultancy, is pitching to council bosses to introduce a network of pipes across the region. These would take captured heat from different sources and transport it to people’s homes potentially cutting down on people’s energy bills by up to 38 per cent. Nicknamed the ‘Bee Network for Heat’, the project could link homes across all ten boroughs in Greater Manchester providing heat to thousands. It is based of a publicly-owned model that has been running in Denmark for decades. A map of the network suggests sources of the heat could come from the Baked Beans factory in Wigan, a bread factory near Bolton, various data centres, a number of different industries, wastewater and sewage treatment works, and the Carrington Power Plant. Another map also suggested Kellogg’s plant near Stretford, heat from mine water near Oldham, and Asda’s distribution centre in Rochdale. At an event on September 30, the we heard a data centre in Heywood could heat the equivalent of 50,000 homes. According to EnergiRaven, enough heat could exist across the region to cover 85% of the regions needs and cut down on household bills by 38%. Over 20 years, they say a heat network could save £8.83bn. At the moment, EnergiRaven say heating costs are currently around 8.7p/kWh but this could fall to 5.4p. While gas heating costs in the UK shot up by £1273, it only rose by £271 in Denmark where homes are part of a district heating network. Those behind the scheme say it will protect homes from energy shocks caused by the wars in Iran and Ukraine by tapping into a UK-energy source. Though the scheme will come at a cost, the UK spent £39.3 billion between October 2022 and March 2023 to subsidise energy costs.

candidates.source_title: 'Beautiful': Derby County prospect rediscovering dangerous best in League Two after challenging 2025/26 season News: The72 - Football League News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Derby County boast a strong academy, although the progression of youth players to the first-team has slowed somewhat in recent years. Among the DCFC alumni of recent seasons are Jayden Bogle, Jason Knight , Morgan Whittaker, Liam Delap and more. The Rams are still producing bright prospects though, and a handful are currently out on loan. Owen Eames has made a good impression at Falkirk having emerged in the senior picture under John Eustace last season. One prospect who started sniffing around the first-team in 2024/25 was Dajaune Brown. And, after a challenging time last season, the striker is finding form in his latest loan away from Pride Park. Nottingham-born Brown made a name for himself in Derby County ’s U18s and U21s, with prolific goalscoring prompting calls for his increased first-team involvement. After a handful of appearances for the Rams, he starred on loan in the National League with Gateshead, where he managed nine goals and eight assists in 22 games. However, injury ended his 2024/25 season early having found a place in the DCFC first-team. He then spent last term on loan at Port Vale , where he managed only three goals and three assists in 34 games as they were relegated from League One. A new loan opportunity came knocking in the summer though, with Rochdale bringing Brown in . He has swiftly found a starting role, and after six goalless games to start, the 20-year-old has found form. Brown was on the scoresheet as the Dale won 2-0 against Oldham Athletic , and he followed that up by scoring one and setting up the other in the 2-1 triumph over Fleetwood Town last weekend. His goal was praised by manager Watson post-game , who said this on Brown: “Yes, beautiful goal. That’s two and two for him. So, [the goals] gives him a lot of confidence.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Tramservices have resumed on the Oldham-Rochdale line after essential track replacement work was successfully completed, marking a major milestone in this summer’s programme of network improvements. It will help deliver a smoother, more reliable service for passengers and support the long-term resilience of the network. Engineers worked day and night between Monsall and Newton Heath & Moston to replace 1.2km of track, improve drainage, renew foundations and correct the alignment and level of the track. It was a big and complex job, using around 290 new concrete sleepers, 2,000 tonnes of gravel and replacing more than 5,000 tonnes of ballast. As a result, sections of the route that previously required speed restrictions can now return to normal operation – up to 50mph on some sections – helping to improve journey times for customers. The most significant being at Trafford Bar and Deansgate-Castlefield. While this work is carried out, there will be no trams on the Eccles, Trafford Centre or Altrincham lines for three weeks from Monday 13 th July to Sunday 2 nd August. Before that, further tram improvement work took place in the city centre . Further work to finish off the job on the Oldham-Rochdale line also took place on Sunday 7 th June and Sunday 12 th July. In regards to the Hopwood Hall Estate Court Case here is my statement as a long standing volunteer. Around 2013, my brother and I became aware that Hopwood DePree had come forward with an interest in saving and restoring his ancestral home. From there, we stayed with the project. My brother and I were involved during its earliest stages and served on the original committee before the official charity was formed. When the project developed and the wider volunteer programme followed, we continued our involvement as volunteers. We were never afraid of getting our hands dirty. We helped with the gardens and grounds, supported restoration activities and assisted at open days, including undertaking security and public-facing duties. Over the years, our voluntary contribution was recognised through a number of awards, something of which we remain extremely proud. For many visitors arriving at Hopwood Hall, my brother and I were among the first people they would meet. We tried to make everyone feel welcome and to represent the project positively. candidates.source_title: Rochdale Council wins 'Downton Shabby' High Court case
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Hopwood DePree published a book called Downton Shabby in 2022 about his efforts to restore Hopwood Hall in Middleton An American man has lost his legal bid to take ownership of a historic mansion for Â£1. Hopwood DePree, who claims ancestral links to the Grade II-listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton, Rochdale, said he was "incredibly disappointed" after a judge at the High Court in Manchester ruled against him. DePree, an actor and filmmaker, argued a 2017 agreement with Rochdale Council gave him the option to buy the manor house after securing planning permission to restore and redevelop it. However, Judge David Hodge KC found the conditions required for ownership of the property to transfer had not been met. Despite its current state, Hopwood Hall was described as being in the top 10% of most important listed buildings in England, the court heard. DePree's plans included a wedding venue, hotel accommodation and visitor attractions aimed at bringing the hall back to life. However, Rochdale Council decided in 2022 not to transfer ownership of the hall to DePree and later locked him and a group of volunteers out of the site.

Nisan Fernando Kurukulasuriya, 39, and of Troutbeck Road, was sentenced to eight months' imprisonment at Manchester Crown Court on Tuesday 15 September. He pleaded guilty to Sexual Assault and Outraging Public Decency at a previous court hearing. He was also handed a 10-year Sexual Harm Prevention Order (SHPO) which will bar him from sitting next to any woman he doesn't know on public transport, and will be on the sex offenders register for 10 years. The court heard how, on Monday 20 April 2026, Kurukulasuriya was on a train from Stoke to Manchester when he sat next to a woman he didn't know who was on the phone. He then sexually assaulted her repeatedly, doing so again even after being pushed away by the woman. The woman then noticed that he had exposed himself and was masturbating in front of her. She shouted at Kurukulasuriya, who in response stood up and ran away to leave the train. The woman immediately got up to report the incident to staff. When the train arrived at Manchester Piccadilly, the woman went to speak to a member of railway staff. Kurukulasuriya meanwhile was stood only a few meters away, seemingly without a ticket that would let him through the gate line. The woman told a member of staff at the gateline that Kurukulasuriya had exposed himself to her, and the member of staff immediately contacted BTP.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: RivingtonHark, on behalf of Rochdale Borough Council, has secured British clothing retailer Peacocks on a long-term lease for a 10,181sq ft unit at Rochdale Riverside, taking the scheme to 92 per cent occupancy. The run of new lettings follows a 15.3 per cent year-on-year footfall increase at Rochdale Riverside, with almost 200,000 visiting during July, continuing an upward year-on-year trend throughout 2026. Following its opening in Spring 2020, Rochdale Riverside has delivered a dynamic mix of shopping, dining and leisure and is at the heart of the wider regeneration of Rochdale town centre. RivingtonHark has asset managed the centre on behalf of the council since 2023. The 200,000sq ft open-air scheme is anchored by a 50,000sq ft M&S store and a six-screen Reel Cinema and is home to leading national retailers including Next, H&M, Boots and JD Sports. Ollie Holland, Asset Manager for Rochdale Riverside at RivingtonHark, said: “The letting brings another nationally recognised retailer to Rochdale Riverside, activating a prominent, centrally located unit and further strengthening the diverse and growing fashion offer. The addition of Peacocks reflects robust demand for well situated space and continued confidence from national and regional occupiers in the long-term appeal of Rochdale Riverside. Rochdale Riverside is another example of how we work closely with local authorities like Rochdale Borough Council to deliver long-term value across town and city centre schemes. With footfall continuing to grow and further lettings in the pipeline we look forward to building on this continued momentum.”

candidates.source_title: What's On Rochdale: Shakespeare, opera, and moving exhibitions - InYourArea
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Find out the latest events from September 30 from All Across the Arts columnist Steve Cooke A treat for Brontë fans coming to Heywood Civic with Jane Eyre. The eponymous heroine’s fight for freedom, happiness and a sense of belonging, blazes from the cruelty of her childhood to the creepy corridors of Thornfield Hall, where she discovers passion, dark secrets, and a love that overcomes every obstacle. Charlotte Brontë’s gothic romance, set against the backdrop of the Yorkshire moors, with a haunting atmosphere and unforgettable emotion, tells a story of independence, resilience, and the courage to follow one’s heart. Brought to life in a new staging by Conn Artists Theatre Company, following on from their recent adaptation of Far from the Madding Crowd, and performed with an ensemble cast of five actors with original music and songs. The powerhouse classical-crossover sensation The Opera Boys have announced their final tour, featuring the world-renowned tenor and very first winner of Britain’s Got Talent, Paul Potts and its coming to the Middleton Arena. Following years of sold-out performances across the globe, The Opera Boys join forces with the man who captured the world’s heart with his legendary audition of “Nessun Dorma”. This collaboration promises an evening of soaring notes, impeccable harmonies, and the perfect blend of opera, musical theatre, and modern pop classics. Paul Potts became a household name in 2007, winning the inaugural season of Britain’s Got Talent. Since then, he has released multi-platinum albums, performed over 1,500 shows in 45 countries, and inspired the Hollywood biopic One Chance.

candidates.source_title: Oktoberfest fears as anti-social behaviour continues in town centre - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Concerns have been raised about this weekend’s Oktoberfest celebrations as large groups of youths returned to Middleton town centre last night. It follows anti-social behaviour over the weekend in which e-bikes and scooters were being ridden illegally, fireworks were set off, and groups of young people wearing balaclavas were intimidating people in the town centre. The ongoing issues led to police introducing dispersal orders for the town centre. Rachel Kennedy shared on Facebook: “I have just walked through Middleton gardens and it’s an absolute disgrace. “The lack of disrespect and the level of abuse we have just experienced is disgraceful.” Keith Bennington added: “Fireworks were being set off at 5pm outside the Arndale. I had two run out in front of my car on Tesco car park on Friday night too.” Middleton Labour group posted: “Scenes of large groups of youths wearing balaclavas riding around on bikes, intimidating people and firing fireworks cannot continue and must stop. “From our multiple meetings, we have learnt that the police heavily go off reporting statics when allocating resources to towns. We therefore urge all residents to report crime and ASB every time you see it, via 101 or online. If the crime is happening now, if anyone is in danger or fireworks are being fired by children, you must dial 999.”
